item.title: Iranian Omani Foreign Ministers hold talks in Muscat
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi, who is visiting Muscat for an official visit to the Sultanate of Oman, met with Omani Foreign Minister Badr Al-Busaidi on Tuesday morning. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran considers the issuance of unjust sentences against a group of Bahraini clerics and citizens on spurious pretexts to be a systematic and widespread violation of human rights and strongly condemns it. The imposition of unjust life and lengthy prison sentences and the confiscation of religious scholars’ property, shortly after the disgraceful remarks made by the US Secretary of State against clerics and prominent figures of the Shia world, demonstrate the Bahraini rulers’ alignment with the US establishment’s efforts to foment religious discord. Undoubtedly, holding show trials and using the judicial system as a cover for the collective punishment and harassment of clerics and ordinary Bahraini citizens can in no way conceal the inhumane nature of this action or its incompatibility with the fundamental principles and norms of human rights. The leveling of entirely baseless and unfounded accusations, including alleged links with Iran, as grounds for the criminal prosecution of Bahraini citizens and their collective sentencing to lengthy prison terms, is a clear indication of the Bahraini rulers’ abuse of the judiciary to suppress any rights advocacy. This, in turn, will undermine the credibility of Bahrain’s judicial system, render the issued verdicts null and void, and further erode the legitimacy and public acceptance of the ruling class in the country. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, while firmly rejecting the baseless allegations leveled against Iran, calls on the Bahraini rulers to end their repression of the people and religious scholars and to respect their human and civil rights in accordance with human rights standards and Islamic teachings. It also emphasizes that a policy of repression and intimidation can in no way prevent the people of Bahrain from pursuing their legitimate and rightful demands.

item.title: Iranian Pakistani Foreign Ministers hold talks in Islamabad
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi, who is in Islamabad to attend the meeting of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO), met with Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar on Monday afternoon. Araghchi thanked Pakistan for its warm hospitality and the successful organization of the 30th meeting of the ECO Council of Foreign Ministers, emphasizing the need to strengthen multilateral cooperation, enhance economic and trade interactions, and expand coordination among member states. The two foreign ministers exchanged views on developing and expanding bilateral relations in areas of mutual interest. Araghchi and Ishaq Dar also reviewed regional and international developments and discussed the latest diplomatic efforts aimed at safeguarding regional stability and security.

Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi met with Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad on Monday afternoon, along with other foreign ministers and senior officials attending the 30th Meeting of the ECO Council of Foreign Ministers. Sharif welcomed the foreign ministers of ECO member states, stressing the importance of strengthening regional cooperation and utilizing the member countries' extensive capacities to expand economic, trade and transit ties among neighboring and regional countries. The foreign ministers thanked Pakistan for hosting the summit and successfully organizing its 30th session, emphasizing the need to strengthen multilateral cooperation, expand economic and trade relations, and promote greater convergence among member states. Araghchi, referring to the productive discussions at the summit, particularly on Palestine and the strong condemnation of the genocide in the occupied Palestinian territories, stressed the urgent need for the international community and Islamic countries to address the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza and the West Bank. Referring to a clause in the summit's final statement supporting Iran's proposed initiative to end the imposed war, Araghchi also praised Pakistan's efforts as a mediator in Iran-US negotiations. item.title: ECO foreign ministers back Iran’s initiative to end US-Israeli imposed war
item.description: The 30th Meeting of the Council of Ministers of Foreign Affairs of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) concluded in Islamabad with the adoption of a final declaration. In one of the paragraphs of the declaration, ECO member states expressed concern over the security situation in the region (due to the US and Israeli regime’s military aggression against Iran). They voiced support for Iran’s recent initiative aimed at bringing the imposed war to a complete and permanent end. Highlighting the importance of diplomatic engagement, they also expressed support for the good offices and mediation efforts of Pakistan and Qatar. The Islamic Republic of Iran recently, as part of its responsible approach to using diplomacy to end the imposed war, conveyed through mediators its two-day plan, which includes Iran’s seven demands and conditions, as well as practical solutions for establishing peace and stability in the region. ECO member states also underscored the Islamic Republic of Iran’s position as one of the founding members of the organization and emphasized its important role in effectively contributing to the advancement of the organization’s objectives.

item.title: Meeting held between Iranian Pakistani Foreign Ministry spokespersons in Islamabad
item.description: Esmail Baqaei, Spokesperson for the Iranian Foreign Ministry, who is accompanying the foreign minister at the ECO Council of Foreign Ministers meeting, held talks with his Pakistani counterpart, Sajjad Haider Khan, in Islamabad on Monday morning. During the meeting, the two sides highlighted the shared historical, civilizational, religious and cultural bonds between the two neighboring Muslim nations and stressed the importance of leveraging the two countries' strong relations and mutual trust to strengthen ties across various fields, including media and culture. The Iranian and Pakistani foreign ministry spokespersons also emphasized the importance of deepening mutual understanding and friendship between the two nations through media and underscored the need to establish appropriate mechanisms to enhance coordination on media-related issues.

item.title: ECO Foreign Ministers’ Council Meeting opens in Islamabad
item.description: The 30th session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) opened in Islamabad on Monday morning, November 16, under the chairmanship of Pakistan’s Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar, with the participation of foreign ministers from member states, including Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi. The meeting, attended by foreign ministers and senior diplomats from ECO member states, will discuss the organization’s efforts to expand economic, trade, transportation, energy, tourism and other forms of cooperation among its 10 member countries. Discussions will also cover agenda programs and ongoing initiatives aimed at strengthening ties among member states. The ECO Vision 2035 document, which seeks to outline the organization’s cooperation prospects over the next decade, will also be reviewed. In addition to representatives of member states, senior officials from several international and regional organizations are attending the meeting, including the Secretary-General of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), the Deputy Secretary-General of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO), and the Director General of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia (CICA). The ECO chairmanship will also be handed over from Kazakhstan to Pakistan at the summit. Pakistan will assume the organization's rotating chairmanship for a two-year term covering 2026–2027. The 30th session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) opened in Islamabad on Monday morning, November 16, under the chairmanship of Pakistan’s Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar, with the participation of foreign ministers from member states, including Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi. The meeting, attended by foreign ministers and senior diplomats from ECO member states, will discuss the organization’s efforts to expand economic, trade, transportation, energy, tourism and other forms of cooperation among its 10 member countries. Discussions will also cover agenda programs and ongoing initiatives aimed at strengthening ties among member states. The ECO Vision 2035 document, which seeks to outline the organization’s cooperation prospects over the next decade, will also be reviewed. In addition to representatives of member states, senior officials from several international and regional organizations are attending the meeting, including the Secretary-General of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), the Deputy Secretary-General of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO), and the Director General of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia (CICA). The ECO chairmanship will also be handed over from Kazakhstan to Pakistan at the summit. Pakistan will assume the organization's rotating chairmanship for a two-year term covering 2026–2027. The Islamic Republic of Iran is scheduled to host the 18th ECO Summit in Tehran in December this year.
